Extract known kin within generation-distance bounds

Source: R/kinship.R
extract_kin.Rd

Find recorded common ancestors within generations parent steps of both an ego and a relative, including each person at distance zero. Uses the same native kinship module as union eligibility. Unknown parents terminate their branches; missing evidence does not establish unrelatedness. At depth two, known parents/children, grandparents/grandchildren, siblings, aunts/uncles, nieces/nephews, and first cousins are included, including half relationships. Great-grandparents and first cousins once removed require depth three.

Usage

extract_kin(population, ego_ids, generations = 2, relative_ids = NULL)

Arguments

population

A hammel_population or a persons data frame, including deceased persons and recorded parent IDs. No known endpoint is required.

ego_ids

Unique person IDs whose known kin should be extracted.

generations

Nonnegative whole number of parent generations on EACH side, default 2. Zero returns no kin between distinct people.

relative_ids

Optional unique relative IDs to consider. NULL means all recorded persons. Unknown IDs are errors; empty vectors return no rows.

Value

A tibble with ego_id, relative_id, common_ancestor_id, ego_distance, relative_distance, ego_lineage, relative_lineage, ego_ancestry_complete, and relative_ancestry_complete. Lineage is "self", "maternal", "paternal", or "both" for shortest routes. Completeness refers only to required parent links within the chosen depth. Empty results retain the same column types; no rows does not prove unrelatedness or complete ancestry. Input ego/relative order is retained; tied ancestor IDs are sorted.

Details

Returns the closest common ancestors by minimum sum of the two distances within the requested bounds. Equally close ancestors have separate rows; count distinct relative IDs when counting people. Does not assign relationship categories or infer full versus half kin from missing links. The ego itself is excluded. Includes deceased and living people in recorded history, without automatic filtering to a census date or living kin. Ancestry cycles are errors.

Examples

persons <- data.frame(person_id = c(10, 20, 30), sex = c("f", "m", "f"),
  birth_time = c(-50, -50, -20), death_time = NA_real_,
  mother_id = c(NA, NA, 10), father_id = c(NA, NA, 20))
population <- hammel_population(persons, end_time = 0)
extract_kin(population, ego_ids = 30)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 9
#>   ego_id relative_id common_ancestor_id ego_distance relative_distance
#>    <dbl>       <dbl>              <dbl>        <int>             <int>
#> 1     30          10                 10            1                 0
#> 2     30          20                 20            1                 0
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: ego_lineage <chr>, relative_lineage <chr>,
#> #   ego_ancestry_complete <lgl>, relative_ancestry_complete <lgl>
